judge-football.justification: Usable (8.3): Monday scout, coach and Combine lines are concrete; film list split into Open first and Flag missed or unproven with named players and a drill for each. Key claim honestly stated as not board-ready (R2 gain intervals include zero; day-3 hit rate 10/15 vs 9/15 for pick order), so the action is a film queue plus a frozen 2026 test. Difficulty (9.0): opportunity and role handled (pick-only, pick-plus-role, full baselines, edge vs interior), class-held-out validation, single-rep reliability 0.43 with measurement-error simulation, drill-vs-NFL turn-radius mismatch (2.7x), thin tracking with no blockers, frozen sha256 rule, multiplicity correction; p=0.10 as best of six sits inside the chance line. Unique (8.4): mapping hoop-drill lean to the same man's NFL corner-turn is a drill-to-game translation; drill half weak (partial rho 0.14, radius-to-radius 0.01). Terminology (8.1): get-off, dip-and-rip, bend, interior vs EDGE, day-3 tape plausible; Hoop G, corner turn, action margin are invented constructs; opening sections statistic-dense; 'Hips there' for Ingram-Dawkins without film support.

Make the Monday action sharper: fixed rule for top third on Hoop G and day-3, expected count of 2026 names flagged, cost of a miss; reconcile the 'strong' NFL half (rho 0.36) with the weak drill half and the 8-name misses.

judge-datascience.justification: Spot-checked numbers reproduce. Strong design: pick-only, pick+role and full no-tracking baselines, nested baseline selection, player-resampled bootstrap within class, pre-stated action margin, best-of-six shuffle null, Holm/BH, errors-in-variables simulation for 0.43 reliability, frozen 2026 test with power. Claims hedged: R2 gains include zero, p=0.10 best of six, 2025 class flat. Weaknesses: Hoop G effect marginal and screened on reused classes; full baseline has negative held-out R2 so headline comparator is weak; NFL-bend chain partial and drill link weak (0.14 [-0.06, 0.32]); reliability 0.43 from two turns of one lap is a proxy. 2.7x drill-vs-NFL radius gap means construct does not transfer geometrically.
top_changes: Add a placebo/negative-control analysis: within-class permuted Hoop G or a non-DL group; report the null slope distribution next to 2.2; fix construction choices beforehand and report the both-turns variant (1.3) as primary sensitivity.

Replace the negative-R2 full baseline as headline comparator with a ridge-shrunk or pick-plus-role baseline chosen before looking at Hoop G; cluster-bootstrap the class-held-out R2 gain; show disattenuated slope (~3.4) as secondary.

Tie the drill-to-NFL chain together with a mediation-style decomposition (Hoop G to NFL bend to pressure) on the same 77 rushers; trace the 1655/132 EPA filter in the appendix (simple rule gives 1681/135).

judge-writeup.justification: check.py passes: 1,904 words, 4 figures, 2 tables. Title states finding with caveat; two-sentence lede then Scout, Coach, Combine bullets. Structure follows finalist pattern; tone honest (R2 gain intervals include zero, p=0.10 after best-of-six, flag missed three worst names). Density is the weak point: Held out by class section stat-heavy (reliability simulation, three robustness bullets, 4-row table, power 52%/87%); jargon remains (partial Spearman rho, Holm, action margin, shrunk, fold-chosen). Why-now motivation thin; why-the-hoop-why-day-3 paragraph overpacked. Headline claim slightly muddled (slope positive, R2 gain not). Hoop G definition plus 0.62/0.18 g values and 2.7x ratio ask reader to hold many numbers.
top_changes: Cut 'Held out by class' to pick-plus-role result and one sentence on others; move 4-row Table 2, fold-chosen row, reliability simulation bullet and power numbers to the appendix; keep robustness as one line each.
Replace jargon (partial Spearman rho, action margin, shrunk, Holm/BH, fold-chosen) with plain language; add a plain-language line under Table 2.

Add a why-now sentence in the first section, split the why-the-hoop-why-day-3 paragraph, and state lede numbers once: +2.2 pressures per 450 rushes per sd [0.4, 3.8], and 10 of 15 vs 9 of 15 vs pick order.
